title: Aetherflux Reservoir on the Hullbreaker engine: the verified kill?

stack.note: cast for {2}; this is cast number 1 this turn — Hullbreaker Horror's trigger and Aetherflux Reservoir's life-gain trigger both fire on every cast

extras.context: Stack 004 (checker: pass) verified the Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet loop: exactly mana-neutral, unbounded casts within one main phase. Stack 005 (checker: pass) confirmed the loop survives with a one-time +1-float exit and that payoffs must key on CAST COUNT, not mana. Aetherflux Reservoir is that payoff: 'Whenever you cast a spell, you gain 1 life for each spell cast this turn' and 'Pay 50 life: Aetherflux Reservoir deals 50 damage to any target.' Three opponents at 34, 40, and 26 life; you at 32. The question is whether the verified engine plus the Reservoir is a complete, rules-verified kill of the whole table in one turn.

scenario.question: With the verified cast loop running and Aetherflux Reservoir on the battlefield: state exactly how much life the Reservoir's trigger nets per loop cycle as the cast count climbs (the arithmetic of 'gain 1 life for each spell cast this turn' on casts n and n+1), how many total casts are needed from a starting life of 32 to pay 50 life three times while surviving, when and how the 50-damage activation is used between loop iterations (it is an activated ability of an artifact — what can opponents do in response, and does Hullbreaker Horror protect it?), and whether killing all three opponents in one main phase is fully supported by these cards alone. State the exact sequence and ledger for the kill, or exactly what falls short.

steps.action: The Hullbreaker trigger and then Arcane Signet resolve (top of stack first), and the 004/005-verified mana-neutral loop runs: each iteration bounces and recasts a rock, adding one cast per iteration. The trigger-sees-n sequencing is FORCED, not chosen: Sol Ring and Arcane Signet are artifact cards without flash, castable only during your main phase while the stack is empty, so every trigger from cast n must have fully resolved before cast n+1 is even legal. The Reservoir trigger for cast #n therefore always resolves seeing exactly n spells cast this turn.
steps.effect: Per-cast life gain climbs: cast n nets +n life (cast n+1 nets +(n+1)). After k total casts the Reservoir has paid out 1+2+...+k = k(k+1)/2 life.

steps.action: Arithmetic bound for the kill: you must pay 50 life three times (150 total), can only pay 50 while at 50 or more life, and must end above 0 (a player at 0 or less loses as a state-based action). From 32 life: 32 + k(k+1)/2 - 150 >= 1 requires k(k+1)/2 >= 119, so k = 15 (120 life gained); k = 14 yields only 105 and fails.
steps.effect: Minimum 15 casts this turn, with the three payments interleaved at points where your life is at least 50 (a legal schedule is given in steps 5, 9, and 10).

steps.action: Hullbreaker Horror and the activation: no protection. Activating an ability is not casting a spell — an ability goes on the stack without a card, and only a card on the stack is a spell — so your Reservoir activation does not trigger Hullbreaker. Nor can you manufacture a trigger in response: the only castable cards in the engine are Sol Ring and Arcane Signet, sorcery-speed artifact spells that are legal to cast only during your main phase while the stack is empty — with the activation (or an opponent's answer) on the stack, no loop cast is legal. On this board, each activation window is fully open; Grand Abolisher (in the 99, not on this battlefield) is the card that would close it during your turn.
steps.effect: The activation can be responded to, and Hullbreaker Horror offers NO protection during any activation window on this board.

steps.action: What the line requires beyond the three loop pieces + Reservoir: nothing. No extra mana (the loop is mana-neutral per stacks 004/005 and the activation cost is life only, paid at activation), and no particular starting life — any positive total works because per-cast gain grows without bound, though from 32 the floor is 15 casts. What interrupts it: any instant-speed answer at any priority window — each of the three activations, and each loop cast, passes priority to every opponent. On this board there is NO protection: the loop's castable pieces are sorcery-speed artifacts, so you can never cast into an occupied stack to trigger Hullbreaker, and Grand Abolisher is not on this battlefield to close the windows.
steps.effect: Complete, rules-supported one-turn table kill on this board: 15 casts, activations after casts 6, 12, and 15, killing the 26-, 40-, then 34-life opponents, ending at 2 life. The rules-level exposure is real: every window is open to instant-speed interaction.

final_state.summary: The kill is complete and fully supported by these cards alone. Exact line: run the verified loop to 6 total casts (life 32 -> 53 via +1..+6), activate for 50 at the 26-life opponent (life 3, they die at -24); loop casts 7-12 (life 60), activate at the 40-life opponent (life 10, dead at -10); loop casts 13-15 (life 52), activate at the 34-life opponent (life 2, dead at -16). 15 casts is the proven minimum from 32 life; the trigger-sees-n count is forced by 301.1 (artifacts are only castable with the stack empty). You win via 104.5 + 104.2a. Caveats: every activation and every loop cast opens a fully open priority window — activating is not casting, so Hullbreaker Horror never triggers during the windows, and the loop's sorcery-speed artifact pieces cannot be cast in response to anything, so Hullbreaker provides NO protection on this board. Opponents here have empty boards, and Grand Abolisher is in the 99 but not deployed.
